topic: Modified personal pronouns and person agreement
claim: CGEL defines pronouns by their exclusion of determiners and treats a he and a she as common-noun uses.
evidence_summary: Halm finds a younger me with myself as the object of ask. The five-year-old you governs was. He also reports first-person plural ourselves with the younger us.
finding: An article-marked NP can show third-person verbal agreement and retain pronoun-specific person information in coreference. A converted-noun analysis needs to explain that split. The distribution in 2002 is open.
proposed_wording: Ordinary personal pronoun NPs exclude determiners. Restricted modified patterns such as the younger me allow an article and can preserve the pronoun’s person features for reflexives.
inference: Can article compatibility decide whether the head has changed category when independent agreement targets diverge?

evidence.source: John Payne and Rodney Huddleston (2002). Nouns and noun phrases. The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language, 323–523.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §10.2, p. 429, treats exclusion of determiners as defining for pronouns. N. 46 assigns he and she with a to the common-noun category.
evidence.example: Poor old me shows CGEL’s limited evaluative modifier pattern. P. 486 [5] gives the ordinary person contrasts in subject–reflexive agreement.
evidence.establishes: Pre-head modification alone is compatible with pronoun status in CGEL. Person agreement provides another test.

evidence.source: Tamás Halm (2022). Modified pronouns and split agreement: the syntax of virtual performatives. NELS 52, 319–329.
evidence.passage: Ch. 5 §10.2, p. 429, treats exclusion of determiners as defining for pronouns. N. 46 assigns he and she with a to the common-noun category.
evidence.example: Questions A Younger Me Would Ask Myself. The five-year-old you was so cute! The younger us were so confident of ourselves.
evidence.establishes: The data show the divergence between verb form and coreferential person. Third-person anaphora also occurs when stages are contrasted. The paper proposes pronominal heads.
